name: Rows
subcategory: spreadsheet databases and operational data apps
tagline: Build connected spreadsheets with a limited set of API-powered cells

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited spreadsheets; 5 AI tasks/month; 10 integration accounts; 3 guests; 500 cell-enrichment operations/month; 500 API calls/month; 1 MB imports; 7-day history.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: 200 AI tasks/month; 10 integration accounts; 10 guests; 1 million cell-enrichment operations/month; 50,000 API calls/month; 5 MB imports; 30-day history; daily refresh.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 1,000 AI tasks/month; 100 integration accounts; 1 million cell-enrichment operations/month; 1 million API calls/month; 100 MB imports; 2-year history; minutely refresh.
tiers.notes: This is the base workspace fee; add $8/member monthly or $6/member on annual billing. The live page says 200 guests in its card/table but 100 in its Q&A.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited AI tasks, integration accounts and guests; starts at 1 million cell-enrichment operations and 1 million API calls/month.

pricing.freeTierCaps: unlimited spreadsheets, 5 AI tasks/month, 10 integration accounts, 3 guests, 500 cell-enrichment operations/month, 500 API calls/month, 1 MB imports and 7-day history
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual cards show $6 instead of $8 per Plus user and $59 + $6/user instead of $79 + $8/user for Pro
pricing.hiddenCosts: Each workspace is upgraded and billed separately; Pro adds a per-member fee on top of the base; members added mid-cycle are prorated; every processed cell consumes an enrichment unit, and AI through the API consumes both API calls and AI tasks; taxes are extra.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Rows, build connected spreadsheets with a limited set of API-powered cells. The hard boundary is integration catalog, formulas, ai, collaboration, and hosted computation, plus data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Build connected spreadsheets with a limited set of API-powered cells, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
whatYouLose: integration catalog, formulas, AI, collaboration, and hosted computation
moatNotes: data model flexibility, collaboration, and integrations
ongoingBurden: schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Rows because teams pay when a flexible database becomes a shared operational system with integrations and years of accumulated business logic. The recurring cost buys schema changes, formulas, permissions, imports, attachments, views, APIs, concurrency, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: NocoDB
priorArt.desc: Active open-source no-code database interface and Airtable alternative.

alternatives.name: Quadratic Personal
alternatives.desc: A real analysis spreadsheet with database connections and programmable cells; API work is less point-and-click than Rows.

facts.engines: Quadratic currently defaults to Claude Sonnet 5 and selects among frontier hosted models; self-hosted deployments can instead bring provider API keys
facts.dataFormat: Spreadsheet files live in Quadratic Cloud and can be downloaded or shared as local files; connected database data remains in the source and query results enter the sheet
facts.gapVsPaid: Quadratic makes database and API work more code- and query-driven, lacking Rows' large catalog of point-and-click integrations and API-powered spreadsheet functions.

alternatives.name: Stackby Free
alternatives.desc: Rows with tables instead of theatre: two live API columns, manual refresh, and 100 automations a month.

facts.engines: AI co-builder is available with low free usage; AI fields/agents require paid plans and can connect to OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google Gemini using user-supplied keys
facts.dataFormat: Stacks and attachments live in Stackby cloud; individual tables/views export to CSV and complete stacks can export to Excel
facts.gapVsPaid: Stackby is a database table with connected columns rather than a full spreadsheet, so cell-level formulas, analysis, and flexible connected calculations are weaker.

alternatives.name: Superhuman Docs Free
alternatives.desc: Connected tables and manual-refresh integrations inside a formula-heavy doc; enough for small live reports, not data engineering.

facts.engines: Superhuman Docs AI is vendor-managed; the provider/model mix is not publicly fixed, and free workspaces receive only trial or limited AI usage
facts.dataFormat: Docs, tables, automations, and attachments live in the vendor cloud on AWS; owned docs export as text/Markdown-like files plus CSV tables, and pages can export to PDF
facts.gapVsPaid: Its connected tables and integrations are less spreadsheet-native and often refresh less automatically, making it weaker for live API-powered financial or operational models.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Rows Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Rows joined Superhuman and now sends new users to Superhuman Docs; not a durable product to adopt today.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Plus plan and a small-team structured database DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Rows in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: build connected spreadsheets with a limited set of API-powered cells, provide grid, form, kanban, and filtered views, and expose a documented API.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create workspaces, bases, tables, fields, records, attachments, relations, and saved views.
Support text, number, currency, date, boolean, select, formula-lite, and relation field types.
Build grid, form, kanban, and record-detail views from one canonical schema.
Add role-based permissions, optimistic concurrency checks, audit history, and trash restore.
Provide CSV import or export and a token-authenticated REST API generated from the schema.
Ship migrations, seed data, backups, health checks, and a schema export format.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out full spreadsheet formula compatibility.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of automations and integrations.
Deliberately leave out large-enterprise governance and vendor-managed scale.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
